The '''AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecture''' is an award and lecture series that "highlights significant contributions of women to applied or computational mathematics."<ref name=":0" /> The [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] (AWM) and the [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] (SIAM) planned the award<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|last=Young|first=Glenys|date=31 July 2015|title=Professor Awarded Distinguished Lecture for Contributions to Mathematics|url=https://today.ttu.edu/posts/2015/07/professor-awarded-distinguished-lecture-for-contributions-to-mathematics|access-date=2021-01-06|website=Texas Tech Today}}</ref> and lecture series in 2002 and first awarded it in 2003. The lecture is normally given each year at the SIAM Annual Meeting.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web|title=AWM-SIAM Sonia Kovalevsky Lecture|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes-recognition/student-prizes/detail/the-awm-siam-sonia-kovalevsky-lecture|publisher=Society of Industrial and Applied Mathematics|access-date=6 January 2021}}</ref> Award winners receive a signed certificate from the AWM and SIAM presidents.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Duraisamy|first=Karthik|date=2017|title=2017 Kovalevsky and Reid Prizes|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319451020|journal=SIAM News|pages=12}}</ref>

The lectures are named after [[Sonia Kovalevsky]] (1850–1891), a well-known [[Russians|Russian]] mathematician of the late 19th century.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|last=Bronston|first=Barri|date=6 July 2016|title=Honoring women in mathematics|url=https://news.tulane.edu/news/honoring-women-mathematics|access-date=2021-01-06|website=Tulane News|language=en}}</ref> [[Karl Weierstrass]] regarded Kovalevsky as his most talented student.  In 1874, she received her Doctor of Philosophy degree from the [[University of Göttingen]] under the supervision of Weierstrass. She was granted ''[[Privatdozent|privatdozentin]]'' status and taught at the [[Stockholm University]] in 1883; she became an ordinary professor (the equivalent of full professor) at this institution in 1889. She was also an editor of the journal ''[[Acta Mathematica]]''.  Kovalevsky did her  important work in the theory of partial differential equations and the rotation of a solid around a fixed point.<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last1=Koblitz |first1=Ann Hibner |title=A Convergence of Lives: Sofia Kovalevskaia: Scientist, Writer, Revolutionary |date=1993 |publisher=Rutgers University Press |location=New Brunswick, New Jersey |isbn=0-8135-1963-2 |pages=305}}</ref>

==Recipients==
The Kovalevky Lecturers have been:<ref>{{cite web|title=Sonia Kovalevsky Lectures|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/kovalevsky-lectures/|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=1 January 2021}}</ref>

* 2004   [[Joyce McLaughlin|Joyce R. McLaughlin]], Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute, “Interior Elastodynamics Inverse Problems: Creating Shear Wave Speed Images of Tissue”
* 2005   [[Ingrid Daubechies]], [[Princeton University]], “Superfast and (Super)sparse Algorithms”
* 2006   [[Irene Fonseca]], [[Carnegie Mellon University]], “New Challenges in the Calculus of Variations”
* 2007   [[Lai-Sang Young]], [[Courant Institute]], “Shear-Induced Chaos”<ref name=":9">{{cite journal |title=Mathematics People: SIAM Prizes Awarded |journal=Notices of the American Mathematical Society |date=October 2007 |volume=54 |issue=9 |page=1164 |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200709/tx070901164p.pdf |access-date=7 January 2021}}</ref>
* 2008   [[Dianne P.
